deterministic_synthesis_analysis.description: Analysis of where deterministic synthesis replaces LLM work in the AutoForge pipeline.

stages_and_synthesis_type.notes: File scanning, LOC counting, technology detection. Pure deterministic.
Dependency graph traversal, subsystem selection. Deterministic.
AST parsing, procedure extraction, entity extraction. Deterministic.
Embedding generation + Qdrant query. Deterministic mechanics, LLM-free.
Planning 195 target components requires architectural reasoning. LLM.
6 LLM calls generate design notes. This is the reasoning layer.
Design notes synthesized into Spring Boot artifacts by deterministic machinery.
Diagnosis requires reasoning about compilation errors. LLM + RAG.
Applying the repair patch is deterministic. LLM provides the content.

areas_where_deterministic_synthesis_shin.notes: No LLM needed for discovering 511 files and 335001 LOC.
Procedures, modules, entities extracted by deterministic parsers.
LLM provides semantic content; deterministic machinery produces Java files, DTOs, interfaces, configs.
Behavioral tests are deterministic HTTP calls.

areas_where_llm_is_genuinely_required.reason: Planning 195 target components requires architectural reasoning.
Each design note captures semantic intent requiring domain understanding.
Understanding compilation failure requires code semantics reasoning.
Constructing the right retrieval query requires understanding information needs.

synthesis_throughput.ratio: LLM takes 9.7x more wall time than deterministic stages
synthesis_throughput.conclusion: The architecture correctly puts LLM effort into the small number of reasoning stages and uses deterministic synthesis for the bulk of artifact generation.

opportunities_for_more_deterministic_syn.status: REJECTED - behavioral tests must verify actual runtime behavior

conclusion: AutoForge already maximizes deterministic synthesis. The LLM is used only where genuine reasoning is required. No further deterministic synthesis opportunities exist without compromising correctness.
